core.title: Route outbound HTTP through the centralized client
core.given: A source file playing a domain, application or presentation role performs, or needs to perform, outbound HTTP
core.when: the agent writes, edits or is responsible for that file
core.then: Make outbound HTTP through the project's centralized, contract-driven client (a client/adapter in the integration role), never via a direct call to the platform's raw HTTP primitive or a bare HTTP-client library.
prefer: Use the project's existing integration-role HTTP client or adapter.
Let that boundary own transport concerns: headers, retries, decoding, error translation.
During GREEN: make only the outbound call and mapping the current acceptance requires.
During GREEN: reuse an existing client or port before a new abstraction; if no compliant boundary exists, add the smallest integration adapter the behavior requires.
avoid: Calling a raw HTTP primitive or bare HTTP-client library directly just to make the test pass.
A generalized HTTP framework for hypothetical endpoints.
Migrating unrelated HTTP callers beyond the one the current acceptance touches.
unless: Test files and the profile's never-scanned trees (vendored/build), which the check does not scan.
Files that the profile's role assignment leaves unassigned (outside the rule, not in violation of it).
core.why: The centralized client holds retries, timeouts, auth headers, tracing and error translation; a bare call site has none of them and never acquires them because nobody remembers it exists. Where a server-rendered fragment depends on an upstream call, a bare call there fails in a way the user sees (for example a blank swap).
evidence: The stack's boundary check reports no bare outbound-HTTP call in the domain-, application- or presentation-role files of the affected source (the affected source satisfies this boundary rule).
The outbound call in the change is made via the integration-role client/adapter (or a port implemented there).
verification: Severity 3; disposition strict — a finding of this rule is a violation, not a warning.

A static source check flags a bare outbound-HTTP call (the profile's bare-call forms) in files of the consumer roles (domain, application, presentation), scanning masked source so occurrences inside strings or comments do not count.
The integration role is excluded — it is the centralized client's own home.
Test files and the profile's never-scanned trees (vendored/build) are not scanned; the exact classification is owned by the stack's checker.
Imports that resolve outside the project graph are not role-checked.
A file that the profile's role assignment leaves unassigned is outside this rule rather than in violation of it.

values: a finding of this rule's boundary check on an in-scope file

fires: An application-role use case needs data from an upstream service and the agent is about to write the call.
A presentation-role handler already contains a bare HTTP-client call to load data for the fragment it renders.
A domain module makes a raw platform HTTP call to look up a remote value.
doesNotFire: An integration-role adapter or the centralized HTTP client itself makes the raw HTTP call.
A test file makes an HTTP call against a test server.
A file in a never-scanned (vendored/build) tree contains a bare call.
A file that the role assignment leaves unassigned contains a bare call.
A bare call appears only inside a string or comment (masked source).

neutralityNotes: The obligation, GREEN-phase preferences, do-not-broaden avoids, evidence and exceptions are fully stack-neutral; the only Bun-only content is the htmx rationale sentence, the detector/validator/finding ids, and the 'fetch'/'axios' task terms. The bare-call forms could not be expressed with an existing vocabulary key (they are call sites, not imports or machinery), so idiom.module_boundaries#bare_http_calls is proposed. bun.json states no concrete file suffixes, so file_kind 'source' vs test instantiates through each stack's file-kind data; in the Bun realization the detector's own classification carries it. 'During GREEN' and the acceptance-test references are ATDD phase vocabulary and assumed shared across stacks.
